name: Patriarchs (Abraham to Joseph)

objectives.text: Identify Abraham as the man God called to leave his home and who believed God's promise
Name Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph in the order they appear in the story of God's family
Retell how God kept his promise to give Abraham and Sarah a son in their old age
Retell the story of Joseph's coat, his brothers' jealousy, and his journey to Egypt
Retell how Joseph revealed himself to his brothers and forgave them
Summarize the call of Abraham and his journey to Canaan
Describe Jacob's dream at Bethel and the promise God repeated to him there
Recall how God renamed Jacob as Israel after Jacob wrestled with him
Describe how the text shows God was with Joseph in Potiphar's house and in prison
Identify the three parts of God's promise to Abraham as land, offspring, and blessing for all nations
Explain how Jacob deceived Isaac and Esau and describe the consequences that followed in his family
Describe Abraham's intercession for Sodom and explain what it reveals about God's justice
Compare Abraham's acts of faith with his failures, such as lying about Sarah and taking Hagar
Explain how God cared for Hagar and Ishmael even outside the line of promise
Trace on a map the movement of the patriarchs from Ur to Haran to Canaan to Egypt
Construct a family tree of the patriarchs including their wives and the sons of Jacob
Explain circumcision as the covenant sign God gave Abraham and how Paul describes it as a seal of faith
Explain the covenant ceremony of Genesis 15 and how God alone passing between the pieces shows the promise rests on him
Explain how Paul uses Genesis 15:6 to teach the Reformed doctrine of justification by faith
Analyze the testing of Abraham in Genesis 22, including God's provision of the ram and the interpretation in Hebrews
Interpret Joseph's statements about God's purpose in his suffering as a teaching on God's providence
Connect the twelve sons of Jacob to the twelve tribes of Israel using Jacob's final blessings
Explain how Judah's change of character and Jacob's blessing on Judah point forward to the kingly line of David and Christ
Explain how Melchizedek's meeting with Abraham is used in Hebrews to portray Christ's priesthood
Explain how Hebrews presents the patriarchs as strangers who lived by faith in promises not yet received
Explain the Reformed doctrine of election as Paul draws it from the choice of Isaac over Ishmael and Jacob over Esau
Evaluate how the Genesis narrator portrays polygamy and favoritism through the conflict they produce rather than by approval
Analyze how ancient Near Eastern customs such as birthright, covenant making, surrogate marriage, and household gods illuminate the patriarchal narratives
Synthesize how the Abrahamic covenant is fulfilled in Christ and extended to the church across redemptive history

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Abraham's call and faith, Joseph's story, Jacob's renaming and deception, Abraham's failures, migration route, Genesis 22, Genesis 50:20, twelve tribes, election, family tree, cultural customs, covenant synthesis). Dropped the vague 'defend providence in preserving the messianic line' as a standalone and folded it into the Joseph providence objective. Moved the family tree earlier to grade 6. Added missing competencies: Isaac's birth, Joseph's forgiveness, Bethel, Joseph in Egypt, the three-part promise, intercession for Sodom, Hagar and Ishmael, circumcision, the Genesis 15 covenant ceremony, justification by faith from Genesis 15:6, Judah's line, Melchizedek, Hebrews 11, and the narrator's treatment of polygamy. Anchored each to specific verses and added confessional references only where they state the doctrine taught.
